rawFindings.title: Dropping `this$N` fields breaks round-tripping of self-referential v1 objects
rawFindings.explanation: The new filter omits every field whose name matches `/^this\$\d+$/`. In Hessian v1, `this$0` is a real serialized reference slot and is required to reconstruct cycles/self-references. For input that encodes an object whose only back-reference is stored in `this$0`, decoding now returns an object with that field missing, so re-encoding or later property access no longer preserves the original graph.
rawFindings.suggestion: Keep storing `this$N` fields in the decoded object, or map them to the decoded reference target instead of skipping them outright.
rawFindings.failureAfterChange: Decoding a v1 buffer for a self-referential object like `ConnectionRequest` now produces `{ ctx: { id: 101 } }` instead of `{ ctx: { id: 101, this$0: <parent> } }`, so the cycle is lost.

rawFindings.title: Dropping `this$N` fields breaks round-tripping of v2 object references
rawFindings.explanation: The same new filter removes v2 synthetic back-reference fields from decoded objects. Those fields are used to preserve object identity in nested/self-referential instances. After this change, a decoded object that contains a back-reference no longer retains that edge, so object graphs with cycles or shared references are flattened incorrectly.
rawFindings.suggestion: Do not skip `this$N` fields during decode; instead preserve them or resolve them to the referenced object before returning.
rawFindings.failureAfterChange: Decoding `v2/object/ConnectionRequest` now yields a structure whose `ctx` object has only `id`, so any subsequent logic expecting the self-reference (or re-encoding the object) cannot reconstruct the original graph.
